stories.title: Subscribe and handle `business_capability_update` webhook for tier changes
stories.description: Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API emits `business_capability_update` events whenever the portfolio's messaging tier limit or the maximum number of allowed phone numbers changes. Rainbow AI currently has no handler for this webhook field, so operators are unaware when the portfolio automatically upgrades or downgrades without polling the Graph API. Handling this event enables real-time admin alerts and automatic tier-record updates.
acceptanceCriteria: The WABA webhook subscription includes the `business_capability_update` field on app startup
A dedicated route handler parses the event and updates the `app_settings` messaging-tier key in the DB
An admin notification is dispatched within 60 seconds of receiving a tier change event
Vitest unit test asserts the handler updates the DB row and emits the notification for a sample payload
technicalNotes: Webhook field name: `business_capability_update` per Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API documentation
Payload includes new messaging limit tier and maximum phone numbers allowed
Pair with existing WABA subscription health check to verify field is registered at startup
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Handle `flows` webhook field for WhatsApp Flows endpoint health events
stories.description: Meta sends `flows` webhook notifications to inform businesses when their WhatsApp Flows endpoint becomes unavailable or recovers, which directly impacts any in-chat form or interactive flow. Without subscribing to this field, Rainbow AI cannot detect Flows endpoint failures and will silently serve broken interactive messages to guests.
acceptanceCriteria: The WABA webhook subscription includes the `flows` field on app startup
A handler logs the event type (endpoint unavailable / recovered) and updates a `flows_endpoint_healthy` flag in `app_settings`
When `flows_endpoint_healthy` is false, any route that would trigger a Flow returns a fallback text message instead
Admin notification is sent when the endpoint transitions from healthy to unhealthy
Vitest test asserts fallback text is returned when the flag is false
technicalNotes: Webhook field name: `flows` per Meta Cloud API documentation
Flows endpoint health events include the Flow ID and failure reason
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Handle `phone_number_quality_update` webhook to track quality rating changes
stories.description: Meta's Cloud API emits `phone_number_quality_update` events when a WABA phone number's quality rating transitions between GREEN, YELLOW, and RED, or when the number is FLAGGED or UNFLAGGED. Rainbow AI does not currently track quality rating, meaning operators discover messaging restrictions (reduced throughput, potential ban) only after delivery failures accumulate.
acceptanceCriteria: The WABA subscription includes `phone_number_quality_update` on startup
Handler persists the new quality rating (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) and event type (FLAGGED/UNFLAGGED) to `app_settings`
Admin notification is sent immediately when rating drops to YELLOW or RED
Admin dashboard quality indicator reflects the stored rating
Vitest unit test asserts the handler persists the rating and sends the notification for YELLOW and RED events
technicalNotes: Webhook field name: `phone_number_quality_update` per Meta Cloud API documentation
FLAGGED status means Meta has imposed a messaging limit downgrade; UNFLAGGED means recovery
Quality rating is evaluated on a rolling 7-day window by Meta
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Portfolio-level messaging limit consolidation: inherit highest tier across all numbers
stories.description: Effective October 7, 2025, Meta changed messaging limits from per-phone-number to per-portfolio: all numbers in a Business Manager portfolio now share the highest tier held by any single number, and new numbers immediately inherit this limit. Rainbow AI's current per-number tier model in `messaging-limits.ts` is architecturally incorrect post this change, which could cause false low-limit alerts and incorrect rate limiting behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: A new `portfolioMessagingLimit` field in `app_settings` stores the single portfolio-level tier
On startup, the system reads the portfolio tier from the DB and uses it for all rate-limit checks rather than per-number tiers
Admin UI displays a single portfolio limit rather than per-number limit fields
Tier upgrade evaluation logic reflects Meta's 6-hour evaluation cycle (not 24-48h)
Vitest test asserts that adding a second phone number inherits the portfolio tier, not a baseline 1K
technicalNotes: Change effective October 7, 2025 per Meta documentation
Meta evaluates tier upgrades every 6 hours based on quality metrics and unique recipient counts
Tier upgrade requires use of at least 50% of current limit within a 7-day window
Reference: https://convrs.io/blog/whatsapp-messaging-limits-updates/ and https://gallabox.com/whatsapp-business-pricing-october-2025-update

stories.title: WhatsApp Business Calling API: inbound call webhook handler and 24h session trigger
stories.description: WhatsApp Business Calling API launched July 1, 2025 and any inbound user-initiated call opens a 24-hour customer service conversation window, the same as an inbound text message. Rainbow AI has no handler for call events, meaning missed calls are not tracked as contact events and the 24-hour session window is not opened, causing loss of follow-up messaging eligibility.
acceptanceCriteria: A webhook handler processes incoming call events and opens/extends the 24-hour session window for the calling JID
Missed calls are recorded in `rainbow_messages` with a `call_missed` message type
Answered calls are recorded with a `call_answered` message type and duration when available
An auto-reply text is sent within the session window when a call is missed (configurable per profile)
Vitest unit test asserts the session window is set and the missed-call record is created
technicalNotes: Calling API launched globally July 1, 2025; requires messaging tier of at least 2,000 business-initiated conversations/day
Business-initiated calls are NOT supported in USA, Canada, Turkey, Nigeria, Vietnam
Inbound user calls open the 24-hour window same as inbound messages per Meta policy
Call recording and call transfer are supported features
Reference: https://respond.io/help/whatsapp/whatsapp-business-calling-api and https://business.whatsapp.com/blog/whatsapp-business-calling-api

stories.title: PDPA Malaysia Phase 3: 72-hour breach notification pipeline to PDPC
stories.description: Effective June 1, 2025 under Malaysia's Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024, data controllers must notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner (PDPC) within 72 hours of discovering a breach that may cause significant harm, and notify affected data subjects within 7 days. Rainbow AI processes personal data (guest names, phone numbers, booking details) and currently has no automated breach detection or notification pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: A breach incident can be logged via a new POST /admin/breach-incidents endpoint with fields: discovery_time, affected_records_count, data_types_affected, likely_harm
The system computes the 72-hour PDPC notification deadline from discovery_time and displays a countdown in the admin dashboard
Breach records are retained in the DB for a minimum of 2 years (matching PDPA requirement)
If the 72-hour deadline passes without the operator marking PDPC notified, an escalation alert is sent to the configured admin contact
A structured breach summary report is exportable in JSON and PDF for submission to PDPC
technicalNotes: PDPA (Amendment) Act 2024 Phase 3 effective June 1, 2025
72-hour window applies to breaches likely to cause significant harm; smaller breaches still require internal logging
Data subject notification must follow within 7 calendar days of PDPC notification
Breach records must be maintained for minimum 2 years per the Act
Reference: https://hhq.com.my/posts/full-implementation-of-the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-final-roundup/

stories.title: PDPA Phase 3: data portability — transfer personal data to third-party controller on request
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA Amendment Act 2024 Phase 3 (June 1, 2025) grants data subjects the right to request transfer of their personal data directly to another data controller of their choice, not just a personal download. This is distinct from the existing machine-readable export story: the system must support controller-to-controller transfer via a signed request and technical feasibility check.
acceptanceCriteria: A POST /admin/data-portability/transfer endpoint accepts: requesting_jid, destination_controller_email, data_types[], and a signed authorization token
The system validates that the request originates from the data subject and records the request with timestamp in the DB
A portability package (JSON, matching existing export schema) is generated and delivered to the destination email within a configurable SLA (default: 30 days)
The data subject receives a WhatsApp confirmation message when the transfer is initiated and completed
Transfer requests and their status are auditable in the admin panel
technicalNotes: PDPA Amendment Act 2024 s.33D requires transfer to be technically feasible and in compatible data formats
The Act does not specify a mandatory timeline for completion; 30-day SLA is a reasonable default pending regulatory guidance
Distinct from machine-readable export (self-download) — this is controller-to-controller transfer
Reference: https://hhq.com.my/posts/full-implementation-of-the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-final-roundup/

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 AA: enforce 24×24 CSS pixel minimum touch target size in webchat widget
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, Level AA, published October 2023) requires all interactive UI elements to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels. The current webchat widget likely has smaller icon buttons (close, send, emoji toggles) that fail this criterion, creating barriers for users with motor impairments or who use touch screens.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive elements in the webchat widget (send button, close button, quick-reply chips, input area) measure at least 24×24 CSS pixels including padding
Automated accessibility audit (axe-core or Playwright accessibility snapshot) reports no 2.5.8 violations in the widget
Inline text links within message bubbles are explicitly exempted per the WCAG exception
Visual regression test confirms button sizes did not regress after CSS changes
technicalNotes: CSS implementation: `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px; padding: 4px;` on all button elements
Exception clause: inline links within text runs are excluded from the 24×24 requirement
Testing tool: axe-core v4.8+ includes a rule for 2.5.8 target size
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/new-in-22/ and https://testparty.ai/blog/wcag-22-new-success-criteria

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 AA: prevent focused elements from being obscured by sticky webchat header
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured Minimum, Level AA) requires that when a UI component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers or fixed footers. The webchat widget uses a fixed header bar that can cover keyboard-focused elements in the message list and input area when users navigate by keyboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard-tabbing through all interactive elements in the webchat widget never leaves a focused element entirely hidden behind the header or footer
CSS `scroll-padding-top` and `scroll-margin-top` are applied to the scrollable message container to account for the fixed header height
Playwright keyboard navigation test confirms all focusable elements are at least partially visible after receiving focus
The fix applies to both desktop and mobile viewport sizes
technicalNotes: CSS fix: `scroll-padding-top: [header-height]px` on the scroll container, `scroll-margin-top: [header-height + buffer]px` on focusable items
WCAG 2.4.11 is Level AA (mandatory); 2.4.12 (Enhanced, AAA) requires zero partial obscuring
Reference: https://testparty.ai/blog/wcag-22-new-success-criteria and https://www.allaccessible.org/blog/wcag-22-complete-guide-2025

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 A: auto-populate previously collected guest data in multi-step webchat forms
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A) requires that information a user has already entered in a process is either auto-populated or available for selection when asked again. When guests provide their name and room number early in a webchat session, subsequent forms (feedback, order confirmation) should not ask for the same information again.
acceptanceCriteria: Guest name and phone/room number collected in one step of a webchat session are automatically populated in subsequent steps without requiring re-entry
The user can still edit auto-populated values before submission
Security-sensitive fields (payment codes, PINs) are exempt and always require explicit entry
Playwright test simulates a two-step flow and asserts the second step has pre-filled values
technicalNotes: Session data should be stored in the conversation context object and passed to each step renderer
WCAG 3.3.7 is Level A (baseline requirement, not just AA/AAA)
Implementation pattern: store collected entities in conversation state and inject into form pre-fill fields
Reference: https://testparty.ai/blog/wcag-22-new-success-criteria

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 A: render webchat help/support access point in a consistent position across all views
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.2.6 (Consistent Help, Level A) requires that help mechanisms—including chat widgets and support contact links—appear in the same relative position across all pages or views where they are present. If the webchat widget launcher or escalation button moves position between different webchat views (main chat, order form, feedback view), it violates this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Talk to a person' / escalation button appears in the same visual position (e.g., bottom-right) across all webchat views
The position is defined in a shared layout component, not duplicated per-view
Playwright visual regression test confirms the button position is identical across the main chat, order confirmation, and feedback views
The fix applies to both desktop and mobile breakpoints
technicalNotes: WCAG 3.2.6 is Level A — baseline mandatory, not optional AAA
Consistent Help applies when the mechanism is repeated across multiple pages/views — single-view widgets are unaffected
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/new-in-22/

stories.title: SSE stream resilience: Last-Event-ID reconnection and token buffer for webchat
stories.description: The webchat widget uses SSE for streaming AI responses but currently does not implement the `Last-Event-ID` header for automatic reconnection, meaning a dropped connection mid-stream forces the user to re-submit their message. Additionally, incomplete SSE frames (split across network packets) are not buffered, causing JSON parse errors on the client.
acceptanceCriteria: Each SSE event is assigned a monotonically increasing `id:` field so browsers can send `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect
The server resumes streaming from the last acknowledged event ID on reconnect within the same conversation session (max 60 seconds)
The client-side SSE parser buffers partial messages (lines not ending with `\n\n`) before attempting JSON.parse()
A dedicated `event: error` frame is sent to the client when the upstream LLM call fails, triggering a user-visible error message without leaving an empty assistant bubble
Playwright test simulates a connection drop mid-stream and asserts the response is completed without user re-submission
technicalNotes: SSE `id:` field enables browser-native reconnection via `Last-Event-ID` request header
Buffer pattern on client: `buffer = lines.pop() || ''` retains incomplete final lines between data chunks
Benchmarks: streaming interfaces feel ~40% faster than buffered even with identical latency
Reference: https://dev.to/pockit_tools/the-complete-guide-to-streaming-llm-responses-in-web-applications-from-sse-to-real-time-ui-3534

stories.title: RAG grounding: constrain AI responses to verified knowledge base and return 'I don't know' for out-of-scope queries
stories.description: Rainbow AI currently allows the LLM to respond from its general parametric knowledge, which can produce plausible but incorrect answers about hostel policies, pricing, and facilities. Implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounding ensures responses are anchored to verified `.rainbow-kb/` content, and the model explicitly declines to answer when the retrieved context does not cover the query.
acceptanceCriteria: For every guest-facing AI response, a retrieval step queries the `.rainbow-kb/` (Pelangi) or `.rainbow-kb-southern/` (Southern) knowledge base and injects the top-3 relevant chunks into the system prompt

The system prompt instructs the model to answer only from the provided context and to respond with a configurable fallback phrase (e.g., 'I don't have that information — please contact us directly') when context is insufficient
Responses that cite a room price, policy, or facility detail must be traceable to a specific KB file in the conversation log
A Vitest semantic test asserts that a query about a non-existent policy returns the fallback phrase and not a fabricated answer
The retrieval latency overhead (embedding lookup) does not exceed 500ms p95
technicalNotes: RAG is the most effective grounding technique per industry consensus; anchors outputs to verified KB rather than parametric memory
Embedding model should match the existing provider (OpenRouter/NVIDIA); use cosine similarity with a minimum relevance threshold (e.g., 0.7)
The `.rainbow-kb/` directory structure is already in place — this story adds the retrieval pipeline, not KB content
Reference: https://sendbird.com/blog/ai-hallucination-detection and https://www.k2view.com/blog/grounding-and-hallucinations-in-ai/

stories.title: Hallucination detection: flag and quarantine AI responses with unverifiable claims before delivery
stories.description: Production AI customer service systems require real-time hallucination detection to prevent incorrect information (wrong prices, non-existent policies) from reaching guests. A detection layer using SelfCheckGPT-style multi-sample consistency checking or a lightweight judge model should intercept responses before sending, routing low-confidence answers to human review.
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable confidence threshold (default: 0.75) is stored in `app_settings`; responses where the model's self-assessed confidence falls below this threshold are not sent directly
Flagged responses are stored in a `flagged_responses` table with: message_id, flagged_reason, confidence_score, conversation_id, and timestamp
Flagged responses trigger a human handoff notification with the flagged content and the original guest message
Admin dashboard displays a 'Flagged Responses' panel showing unresolved flags with resolution actions (approve, edit, escalate)
Vitest test asserts that a deliberately low-confidence prompt results in a flag record and handoff notification, not a direct reply
technicalNotes: SelfCheckGPT approach: generate 2-3 response samples for the same query and compare consistency; divergence indicates hallucination risk
Alternative: instruct the LLM to output a confidence field in a structured JSON response before the actual reply text
Sendbird's production implementation uses near-zero-latency webhook alerts for flagged content
Reference: https://sendbird.com/blog/ai-hallucination-detection

stories.title: Confidence-score based automatic chatbot-to-human escalation with context bundle
stories.description: Industry best practice requires AI chatbots to automatically escalate to human agents when the model's confidence in its response drops below a configurable threshold, rather than delivering a potentially wrong answer. This complements the existing sentiment-based escalation by adding a model-internal signal, and requires passing a structured context bundle to the receiving agent.
acceptanceCriteria: A confidence score (0.0-1.0) is extracted from each AI response (via structured output or a secondary judge call)
When confidence falls below a configurable threshold (default: 0.65, stored in `app_settings`), the conversation is escalated to human review instead of auto-replied
The escalation context bundle includes: last 10 messages, extracted entities (guest name, room, issue type), confidence score, and the draft AI response that was withheld
The guest receives a holding message ('Connecting you with our team...') within 5 seconds of the escalation trigger
Repeated low-confidence escalations from the same intent category are logged for KB gap analysis
Vitest test asserts escalation fires and the withheld draft is included in the context bundle
technicalNotes: Threshold configurable per-profile to allow different sensitivity for Pelangi vs Southern
Context bundle format should be JSON-serializable and storable in `escalation_events` table
Escalation triggers should include: confidence below threshold, 3+ consecutive misunderstood queries, explicit user request, and sentiment threshold (existing)
Reference: https://cobbai.com/blog/chatbot-escalation-best-practices and https://www.replicant.com/blog/when-to-hand-off-to-a-human-how-to-set-effective-ai-escalation-rules

stories.title: Meta AI bot compliance: enforce concrete business task scope and reject open-ended AI chat
stories.description: Meta tightened AI chatbot rules in 2026, requiring that bots on WhatsApp Business perform concrete business tasks (answering support questions, booking, purchase advice) and prohibiting open-ended conversational AI without a clear business purpose. Rainbow AI should validate that its system prompt explicitly scopes the bot to defined tasks and reject or redirect queries outside its business domain.
acceptanceCriteria: The system prompt for each profile explicitly lists the permitted task categories (e.g., check-in enquiry, booking status, menu ordering, general property FAQ)
An out-of-scope classifier (rule-based or LLM-assisted) detects queries that fall outside the permitted task categories and returns a polite redirect rather than attempting to answer
Out-of-scope query types are logged in `intent_analytics` with a new `out_of_scope` intent category
Admin UI allows operators to configure the permitted task list per profile
Vitest test asserts that a clearly off-topic query (e.g., 'write me a poem') triggers the out-of-scope handler
technicalNotes: Meta's 2026 policy requires bots to perform 'concrete business tasks' — open-ended AI chats without a clear goal are disallowed
Out-of-scope detection can use a lightweight intent classifier before the main LLM call to avoid token cost
Permitted task categories should be stored in `src/assistant/data/settings.json` and loaded at startup
Reference: https://chatarmin.com/en/blog/whats-app-business-api-integration

stories.title: WhatsApp marketing message user-level frequency cap: enforce 2-message-per-day limit
stories.description: Meta enforces a cross-brand marketing message frequency cap where individual WhatsApp users can receive a maximum of approximately 2 marketing template messages per day across all businesses. Rainbow AI has no per-user daily marketing send counter, meaning bulk promotional sends (e.g., cafe specials, hostel promotions) may silently fail delivery for users who already received marketing from other businesses that day.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-JID daily marketing send counter is maintained in Redis or the DB, resetting at midnight UTC
Before dispatching a marketing template, the system checks the counter and skips the send (with a logged reason) if the JID has already received 2 marketing messages that day
Skipped sends are recorded in a `skipped_sends` table with reason `frequency_cap` for operator review
A daily summary shows how many sends were skipped due to frequency cap across all profiles
Vitest test asserts the third marketing send to the same JID within 24 hours is skipped and logged
technicalNotes: Meta's frequency cap is ~2 marketing messages per user per day across all businesses; exact cap may vary by region
Delivery failures due to frequency capping appear as delivery errors rather than explicit cap notifications
The counter should be separate from the existing per-JID rate limiter (which governs all message types)
Reference: https://chatarmin.com/en/blog/whats-app-messaging-limits and https://gallabox.com/whatsapp-business-pricing-october-2025-update

stories.title: Webchat widget conversational order flow with delivery status push notifications
stories.description: Industry best practice for F&B conversational commerce requires automated push notifications for order status updates (confirmed, preparing, out for delivery, delivered) to be sent within the same WhatsApp or webchat session. Makan Moments Cafe currently receives orders but does not send structured status updates back to the customer after confirmation, reducing trust and increasing inbound status enquiry volume.
acceptanceCriteria: After an order is confirmed by the kitchen (via POS webhook), a status message is automatically sent to the customer's webchat/WhatsApp session within 60 seconds
Status messages cover at minimum: order received, order being prepared, order ready/dispatched
Each status message includes the order ID and an estimated time where applicable
Customers can type 'order status' or 'where is my order' to receive the current status without operator intervention
Status update delivery is logged in `rainbow_messages` with a `order_status_update` message type
technicalNotes: WhatsApp 98% open rate and 80% read-within-5-minutes make it the ideal channel for time-sensitive order status updates
Status push can be triggered by the existing POS webhook receiver (US-876) which already receives KDS confirmations
Use Utility template category for transactional status messages (lower cost than Marketing)
Reference: https://reelo.io/blog/whatsapp-marketing-for-restaurants-the-ultimate-guide and https://www.verloop.io/blog/whatsapp-business-restaurants/

stories.title: PDPA Phase 3: DPO contact details surfaced in-product within 24 hours of a data processing interaction
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA Amendment Act 2024 Phase 3 (June 1, 2025) requires organizations processing personal data of more than 20,000 data subjects (or 10,000 sensitive records) to appoint a Data Protection Officer and make the DPO's contact details available. Rainbow AI processes guest personal data across multiple hospitality properties but does not currently surface DPO contact information to data subjects at the point of data collection.
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable `dpo_contact` field (name, email, phone) is stored in `app_settings` per profile

Within 24 hours of a guest's first data-processing interaction (check-in enquiry, order placement, registration), a WhatsApp or webchat message includes the DPO contact details and a data protection summary
The DPO contact message is distinct from the existing consent banner and is delivered as a separate informational message
Admin UI allows operators to configure DPO contact details and toggle the disclosure feature per profile
Vitest test asserts the DPO disclosure message is queued on a new guest's first interaction
technicalNotes: DPO appointment is mandatory if processing data of 20,000+ data subjects OR sensitive data for 10,000+ data subjects OR conducting systematic monitoring
PDPA Phase 3 effective June 1, 2025
DPO contact disclosure should reference the data processing purposes in accordance with PDPA s.6
Reference: https://hhq.com.my/posts/full-implementation-of-the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-final-roundup/
